scope: Five adversarial judge objections to the current Intel SHORT research recommendation. Existing forecasts and values only; no new valuation, probability, deck or submission.
verdict: Defensible as an owned, moderate-conviction investment judgment suitable for an initial screen. It is not a demonstrated robust mispricing. The argument needs to explain capital returns and the preference for slower absorption, and disclose both the funded faster recovery and the unvalued major external-foundry option. The weakest defense is price convergence timing.

objections.judge: Why penalize growth investment? Intel is buying assets that will generate years of cash.
objections.answer: Growth investment creates value when its later operating cash justifies its cost. The model credits the resulting revenue and earnings while charging the investment once. Its funded faster-recovery case spends an additional 11B on physical capital and 4B on working capital, yet raises the end-2030 value from 47.99 to 57.12 at the same 12% rate. That is positive modeled investment value. The short rests on the preferred recovery and continuing investment burden yielding less stock value than the 60.55 reference price, not on a claim that capex is inherently harmful.
objections.concession: We have not established a project-by-project negative NPV or shown that every future investment earns below its cost of capital.
objections.remove: Large capex destroys shareholder value; growth spending is a loss; stronger sales cannot improve the valuation.

objections.judge: Investors already know about 2027 cash burn. Why should the stock fall within three to five years?
objections.answer: The disputed outcome is the cash recovery after the investment year. I expect 2027-2029 reports to show accepted server shipments rising while underlying Foundry profit and pre-financing owner cash improve more slowly than a rapid-absorption investment case requires. Those reports progressively reveal whether higher revenue needs continuing fresh tools, supplier advances and process spending. That is my expected route to reassessment. The 47.99 end-2030 endpoint represents a conditional 20.75% price decline before short carrying costs; it is not a probability-weighted return or a dated catalyst.
objections.concession: No financing deadline forces convergence: the forecast retains substantial liquidity and needs no new borrowing. The stock can retain a large future-growth premium despite the operating path. Lack of an announced catalyst reduces conviction and timing control; it does not make a fundamental short impossible.
objections.remove: An imminent cash crisis or forced equity raise will cause the decline; known 2027 cash burn is new information; the DCF guarantees convergence by 2030.

objections.judge: Your short ignores the option on large external 14A customers. Why should that option be worth zero?
objections.answer: It should not be asserted worthless. The central forecast funds ongoing internal node development and allows Foundry profitability later, but includes no separate major external-customer program or explicit option premium. A successful external program could add material value, especially where it uses already funded infrastructure. It would also require specified demand, ramp timing, incremental capital and economics. The 47.99 value must therefore remain labeled as conditional on the modeled operating scope. The investment judgment is that unannounced external business does not yet outweigh the capital-return concern at the reference price; that is a forecast judgment, not an identified zero option value.
objections.concession: The existing work does not provide a complete probability-weighted valuation of major external-foundry wins. A credible committed customer with attractive funded economics requires re-underwriting and can invalidate the short before revenue appears.
objections.remove: No named customer means zero option value; the funded bull exhausts all upside; 47.99 is an exhaustive option-adjusted intrinsic value.

objections.judge: Almost half your operating value comes after 2040. Is the short just a discount-rate and terminal-capital assumption?
objections.answer: Long-run capital returns are a material part of the thesis: 48.6% of the base end-2030 operating value is cash after 2040. The model explicitly funds replacement and growth and uses a prospective 12% nominal unlevered operating rate selected before its first equity output, with 3% terminal growth. Mature incremental capital turnover of 0.60 is an owned judgment, not an empirically measured coefficient. The sensitivity is material and disclosed: funded faster recovery is worth 57.12 at 12% and 63.74 at 11%. A judge who expects materially better capital productivity or lower asset risk can reasonably disagree with the short.
objections.concession: The near-term substrate evidence cannot by itself establish perpetual capital intensity. The forecast and price are conditional estimates, not engineering bounds or precise measurements.
objections.remove: The target is insensitive to long-run assumptions; current factory utilization empirically calibrates mature incremental turnover; an arithmetic audit validates the economic forecast.

objections.judge: Existing factories can be reused and your faster case is funded. Why prefer the slower base?
objections.answer: I expect existing-site upgrades and process learning to improve output. I prefer slower profit absorption because the product and manufacturing economics improve at different speeds: richer CPU selling prices largely benefit Products, while weak client loading, distinct process capacity, complete-package constraints, new depreciation and continuing 14A development still burden Foundry. Q3 already combined substantial same-node cost progress with a roughly 1.9B Foundry loss; the filing identifies lower period and inventory-related charges among the improvements. This supports a gradual recovery without mechanically extending one quarter. Physical reuse makes 2028 breakeven a serious countercase, but does not by itself resolve profitability after all those costs.
objections.concession: This is a comparative forecast judgment, not a measured probability. The physical evidence gives the faster 2028-2029 absorption mechanism meaningful support, particularly from Ireland and Fab 52.
objections.change_view: Late-2027 underlying quarterly Foundry losses approaching 0.5B or less, alongside the accepted-output ramp and spending within the funded envelope, would favor 2028 breakeven and trigger an immediate revision. The 0.5B checkpoint is an owned monitoring threshold, not management guidance. Do not wait until 2030.
objections.remove: All growth requires new greenfield fabs; Fab 62 certainly produces nothing before end-2028; the faster case requires a technological miracle.

common_guard: Current Morningstar and INH commentary already recognizes capital spending and supply constraints. Do not attribute their valuation differences to omitted capital, a specific capital-turnover assumption or market ignorance without their matched forecasts.
